desc:
A web app redesign for better usability makes an existing app easier to understand and finish tasks in, without throwing away the code behind it. Ecom Swift LLC reviews your screens, redesigns the flows that cause trouble and builds the changes into your app.

## What is a web app redesign?

A web app redesign changes how an existing application looks and guides people, while keeping its core features and data. It covers layouts, labels, buttons, spacing, colors, forms and the order of steps in a task. A redesign is not a rebuild: the engine stays, and the controls and screens are improved.

This is often the most economical way to improve a product that works but frustrates the people using it.

## Why do users struggle with older apps?

Apps grow in layers. Each new feature gets squeezed onto an existing screen, labels reflect internal jargon, and buttons multiply. After a while, the person trying to complete a simple task must guess where to click. Screens designed for desktop become cramped on phones, and inconsistent styling makes the product look neglected.

Struggling users contact support, make mistakes, skip features or quit. Most never explain why. The cost shows up as extra support work, abandoned tasks and a product that feels harder to sell.

## How a redesign affects your results

Clearer screens help people reach their goal in fewer steps and with fewer errors. That can mean more completed sign-ups, orders or tasks, fewer questions to your support team and faster training for new staff. A consistent look also builds confidence in a product, which matters when you ask for payment or personal data.

We cannot promise a particular lift, since that depends on your users and what was wrong. What we can do is find the likely causes of confusion, fix them and show you the change in the key flows through before and after comparisons.

## What a great redesign includes

- A usability review of your most important screens, with notes on what trips people up.
- A focus on the flows that matter most, such as sign-up, checkout or task completion.
- Plain wording on labels, buttons and messages.
- Clear visual hierarchy, so the main action on each screen stands out.
- Spacing, type and color cleaned up into one consistent style.
- Mobile layouts that fit small screens properly.
- Better empty states, errors and confirmations.
- Before and after mockups that show exactly what will change.
- Changes built into your app, not only delivered as pictures.
- A shared style guide and components for larger refreshes.

## What we do

We start by walking through your app as a new user would and listing the points of friction. We talk with you about who uses it and what they are trying to do. Then we sketch changes, show them to you and refine them. Once agreed, the new designs are built into your existing code.

The Basic package reviews several screens, redesigns two of them, improves labels and buttons, fixes mobile layouts and delivers before and after mockups. Standard redesigns more screens, reworks one key flow, builds the new styles into your app and cleans up spacing, type and color, with a review call. Premium redesigns a larger set of screens and several flows, adds a shared style guide and components, applies accessibility fixes on updated screens, refreshes onboarding and ends with a handover call. Add-ons include extra screens, a click-through prototype and an icon set refresh.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Tell us where users complain or give up.
- Share support questions and any feedback you already have.
- Choose one or two flows to improve first.
- Keep your existing data and features in place.
- Check the changes on a real phone before release.

**Avoid:**
- Redesigning everything at once, which makes problems hard to trace.
- Changing familiar navigation without a clear reason.
- Judging the design only by taste rather than by task success.
- Hiding useful features to make screens look cleaner.
- Forgetting to tell existing users what has changed.

## Who it is for

This service suits an owner whose app works but gets complaints about being confusing, a team that inherited a product with inconsistent screens, and a founder who needs the product to look credible before a launch or a pitch. It also suits those who cannot afford a full rebuild.

## What we need from you

Send a link or login to a test account, a list of the screens or flows that bother you most and any feedback you have gathered. Code access helps if you want the changes built in. We never ask for passwords. Access is given as a collaborator, team or developer user, and you can end it whenever you choose.
